- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.7) and forecast is significantly above recent history, reduce forecast by 5–10% to avoid over-optimism.  
- If sentiment is negative (≤ -0.3) and forecast is above recent mean, apply downward bias of 3–8% to reflect bearish sentiment.  
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > +10% above recent peak), reduce forecast by 10–15% in next 3–5 days to avoid overshoot.  
- If forecast is consistently above true outcome over 5+ days with no clear trend reversal, apply mean reversion correction: subtract 1–3% per day until convergence.  
- For 30-day horizon, if sentiment is volatile (±0.35 or more in 3 consecutive days), reduce forecast volatility by 20–30% to avoid overfitting to noise.  
- When sentiment is neutral (0.2–0.6) and forecast is > 5% above recent 10-day average, flag for downward adjustment to prevent false momentum.
